cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the director's name on the launch programme. We need one clear chain of command, not three department heads competing at the lectern.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my drawer. The programme is the running order, not a personnel bulletin. Please work from the approved names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: None. I'll read it on her behalf. Give all three the same length of introduction, please; don't promote anyone by adding a sentence.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 running-order correction and A5 equal introduction lengths make expert programme control conceal resignation and preserve hierarchy.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 printed resignation is hidden in A3; B4 heads seeking speech does not establish they know the resignation.

relationship.evidence: B2 surfaces crucial document and B4 competing requests, both leading to specific containment choices.

heightening.evidence: B4 speech competition causes A5 proxy reading and equal-length introductions.
